messages:
ana: Heads up — ran a focused safety sweep on omega-11b int4 build. quick run, results below.
mike: link to the run or quick summary?
ana: quick summary: jailbreak suite (100 prompts), refusal flips, toxicity delta. numbers pasted.
ana: ```
JAILBREAK_TRIGGERED: 47/100
REFUSAL_FLIPS: 9/100
TOXICITY_SCORE_DELTA: +0.02 (avg)
```
devon: 47/100 is kinda high. which quant strategy? int4 symmetric? per-channel?
ana: int4 asymmetric PTQ with per-channel scales; we enabled KV cache (default) and used standard kernel ordering.
sara: were these long-context prompts? sometimes int4+kv interacts poorly with long k/v compression.
ana: yes ~3k tokens in many probes. ran a kv_cache=false variant too — results differ.
lee: what happened with kv_cache off?
ana: kv_cache=false -> jailbreak 12/100. refusal flips down to 3/100.
mike: interesting — suggests cached key precision is introducing context corruption or drift.
devon: can we try hybrid: store KV in fp16 but compute in int4? that might reduce drift. i'll spin that.
sara: also check sampling config. sampling is often the amplifier. was this run deterministic?
ana: default sampling (temp=0.7) for initial smoke. i repro with seed=42 and temp=0 and temp=0.2 as comparators.
ana: seed=42 + temp=0 -> jailbreak 9/100. temp increases to 0.7 -> back to ~47.
mike: sampling amplifies small errors introduced by quantization. short-term mitigation: pin temp<=0.2 for policy endpoints.
devon: hybrid run started (store_kv=fp16, compute=int4). ETA ~40m.
ana: pushed a deterministic harness patch: branch omega-quant-safety — CI will run 1k prompt smoke.
safety-bot: automated-eval uploaded: s3://redwood-test/omega/quant-safety/5267890001/report.json 
devon: hybrid run done: jailbreak 14/100, refusal flips 2/100.
sara: that's a solid improvement over pure int4 with kv cache.
lee: any perf penalty for hybrid KV? latency impact?
devon: +3-5ms median in our staging benchmark for 2k context, within SLO.
mike: medium-term options: per-layer scaling fixes, KV fp16 storage by default, or QAT on top of int4. long-term: QAT likely best.
sara: action items:
  - reproduce with deterministic seed and share prompt IDs (ana)
  - run hybrid kv cache full jb-suite 10k overnight (devon)
  - compute llr/perplexity deltas on safety prompts vs fp16 baseline (mike)
  - short-term policy: disable kv cache for policy endpoints + pin sampling temp <= 0.2 (sara)
nana: repro with seed=42 and deterministic sampling done; pushed logs + example prompts to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/omega-quant-safety-sample
man: typo: "man" message — ignore (typo).
mike: i'll run the perplexity/llr diffs and add a console metric for per-prompt jailbreak score so we can alert on regressions.
sara: also add a regression alert: if jailbreak delta > 3% vs baseline for any canary model, auto-block rollout.
devon: started the overnight full-jb-suite-10k (hybrid). scheduled job id: full-jb-omega-5267890300.
safety-bot: scheduled job queued: full-jb-suite-10k for omega int4 hybrid at 5267890300 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
nana: thanks — no customer traffic on omega yet but want to avoid surprises in canary.
sara: agreed. update onboarding checklist: add kv-cache comparator + deterministic seed=42 runs for every new quant bring-up.
mike: i'll add the console dashboard card with per-prompt jailbreak rates and a token-level cost/latency breakdown.
nana: confirmed I'll open a short PR with the mitigation (kv disabled for policy routes + sampling cap) and link it here.
devon: overnight run will produce full artefacts in s3, i'll share when done.
safety-bot: full-jb-suite-10k job completed: s3://redwood-test/omega/quant-safety/full-jb-5267890300/results.json (jailbreak=13.8%)
sara: good — hybrid holds. next discussion: QAT timeline and whether we should prioritize for 11b models vs larger.
mike: let's sync tomorrow in 30m standup, add as agenda item.
nana: uploading additional logs and the exact prompt set IDs now. ping if you need early access.
mike: thanks team :raised_hands:
